context: The RDD framework needs comprehensive test coverage for core components in the .rdd/ directory. Current tests cover build, install, and some Python modules, but many are obsolete after recent framework changes. The goal is to create new tests for action scripts, configuration validation, and integration workflows while enhancing the existing test infrastructure with selective execution capabilities.

questions.question-text: Should we preserve any existing tests in tests/python/ or completely replace them with the new test suite?

options.label: Complete replacement - Delete all existing tests in tests/python/ and start fresh
options.pros: Clean slate, ensures consistency with new framework structure, no legacy test maintenance burden, simpler to implement
options.cons: Loses any valid test coverage that might still be relevant, no gradual migration path, higher initial effort

options.label: Selective preservation - Keep tests that are still valid and complement with new tests
options.pros: Preserves working test coverage, gradual migration approach, can identify what's still valuable
options.cons: Requires careful analysis of each existing test, potential inconsistency between old and new tests, more complex initial work

options.label: Hybrid approach - Archive existing tests in a separate folder and build new suite from scratch
options.pros: Preserves old tests for reference without mixing them, clean new structure, easy rollback if needed
options.cons: Duplicate test organization overhead, archived tests may never be used, confusion about which tests to run

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states 'It is OK to replace all the tests - a lot of the code was changed as building a new version and there is no user impact yet.' This indicates a complete replacement is acceptable and preferred. Starting fresh ensures tests match the current framework architecture without legacy baggage.

questions.question-text: How should we organize the new tests in tests/rdd-framework/?

options.label: Flat structure - All test files directly in tests/rdd-framework/
options.pros: Simple structure, easy to navigate, no nested folders to manage
options.cons: Can become cluttered with many test files, harder to find specific test categories

options.label: Component-based subdirectories - tests/rdd-framework/actions/, tests/rdd-framework/config/, tests/rdd-framework/integration/
options.pros: Clear organization by component, scalable, mirrors the source code structure, easier to run specific test categories
options.cons: Slightly more complex navigation, requires maintaining folder structure

options.label: Type-based subdirectories - tests/rdd-framework/unit/, tests/rdd-framework/integration/
options.pros: Clear separation by test type, aligns with test execution flags (--unit, --integration), common pattern in many projects
options.cons: Doesn't mirror source structure, harder to find tests for specific components

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt mentions 'tests/rdd-framework/ with component subdirs' and emphasizes testing action scripts, configuration, and integration workflows separately. Component-based organization makes it easy to locate tests for specific framework parts and supports the selective execution requirements (--actions flag). It also mirrors the .rdd/src/ structure for consistency.

questions.question-text: What mocking strategy should we use for unit tests of action scripts?

options.label: Python unittest.mock - Use standard library mocking throughout
options.pros: No external dependencies, well-documented, familiar to most Python developers, part of standard library
options.cons: More verbose than some alternatives, can be complex for nested mocking scenarios

options.label: pytest-mock - Use pytest's mocking fixture wrapper around unittest.mock
options.pros: Cleaner syntax than unittest.mock, integrates well with pytest, less boilerplate code
options.cons: Additional test dependency, learning curve for developers unfamiliar with pytest-mock

options.label: Hybrid - Use temporary directories for filesystem operations, mock only external calls
options.pros: More realistic testing, catches real filesystem issues, less mocking complexity
options.cons: Slower test execution, more complex cleanup, can be flaky on different filesystems

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt states 'Unit tests with heavy mocking' which indicates mocking is preferred over real filesystem operations. pytest-mock provides cleaner syntax while the framework already uses pytest as the test runner (mentioned in requirements). This balances developer experience with testing best practices.

questions.question-text: Should integration tests use a shared temporary .rdd-instance-test/ directory or create unique directories per test?

options.label: Shared directory - Single .rdd-instance-test/ cleaned before each test run
options.pros: Simpler setup, easier to inspect test state after failures, less filesystem churn
options.cons: Cannot run tests in parallel, risk of state leakage between tests, cleanup failures affect all tests

options.label: Unique per-test directories - Each test gets .rdd-instance-test-<uuid>/ or similar
options.pros: Complete test isolation, supports parallel execution, no cleanup dependencies between tests
options.cons: More complex cleanup logic, harder to debug (many directories), slightly slower due to repeated setup

options.label: Per-test-suite directories - Each test file gets its own directory, shared within that file
options.pros: Balance between isolation and complexity, supports file-level parallelization, easier debugging than per-test
options.cons: Still has some state leakage risk within test files, more complex than single shared directory

questions.recommendation-rationale: Integration tests validate critical workflows end-to-end and need complete isolation to prevent test interference. Unique directories per test enable parallel execution (faster CI/CD) and ensure each test starts with a clean state. pytest's tmp_path fixture makes this pattern straightforward to implement.

questions.question-text: How should the enhanced test runner handle coverage reporting for selective test execution?

options.label: Always measure full coverage - Coverage includes all .rdd/src/ code regardless of which tests run
options.pros: Consistent coverage metrics, shows impact of each test category on overall coverage, easier to track coverage trends
options.cons: Misleading when running subset of tests (shows low coverage even if selected tests are well-covered), slower execution

options.label: Selective coverage - Coverage measured only for code tested by the selected test category
options.pros: Accurate coverage for the selected scope, faster for targeted test runs, clear metrics per component
options.cons: Harder to track overall project coverage, requires careful configuration of coverage scope per flag

options.label: Dual reporting - Provide both selective and full coverage, let user choose via --coverage-scope flag
options.pros: Maximum flexibility, supports both use cases, useful for both development and CI/CD
options.cons: More complex implementation, potential confusion about which metric to trust, longer execution time

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt specifies selective execution flags (--actions, --rdd-framework, etc.) to support focused development workflows. Selective coverage aligns with this philosophy - developers running --actions tests want to see coverage of action scripts, not unrelated modules. CI/CD can still run all tests for full coverage metrics.

questions.question-text: Should we modify .github/workflows/tests.yml to explicitly run the new RDD framework tests?

options.label: No modification - Default 'run all tests' behavior already covers new tests
options.pros: Follows the prompt constraint 'Do NOT modify unless adding new test categories', simpler implementation, less CI/CD changes
options.cons: No explicit visibility of RDD framework test execution in CI/CD logs, harder to identify which test category fails

options.label: Add RDD framework test step - New CI/CD step that explicitly runs python scripts/run-tests.py --rdd-framework
options.pros: Clear visibility in CI/CD logs, can track RDD framework test results separately, easier debugging of CI/CD failures
options.cons: Modifies CI/CD workflow (needs justification), slightly longer CI/CD execution if tests run twice

options.label: Add test category matrix - Run each test category (build, install, python, rdd-framework) as separate CI/CD jobs
options.pros: Parallel execution (faster CI/CD), granular failure reporting, easy to see which category failed
options.cons: Significant CI/CD changes, more complex workflow file, longer overall workflow (parallel but more jobs)

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states 'Do NOT modify .github/workflows/tests.yml unless adding new test categories'. Adding RDD framework tests doesn't constitute a new test category - it's part of the existing Python tests. The default 'run all tests' behavior will execute the new tests in tests/rdd-framework/ automatically.

questions.question-text: What should be the priority order for implementing test coverage if time is limited?

options.label: Action scripts first - Focus on achieving 80% coverage for all .rdd/src/actions/*.py files before other components
options.pros: Targets the highest-risk area (most complex logic), aligns with success criteria, immediate value for critical workflows
options.cons: Leaves config validation and integration tests until later, may miss system-level issues

options.label: Integration workflows first - Build end-to-end tests for critical workflows, then fill in unit tests
options.pros: Validates core user journeys early, catches integration issues, provides confidence in full system
options.cons: Doesn't meet the 80% action script coverage requirement initially, integration tests are slower to write

options.label: Balanced approach - Implement tests for one complete workflow (unit + integration) at a time
options.pros: Provides both depth and breadth, ensures each workflow is fully tested, incremental progress
options.cons: May not reach 80% coverage requirement quickly, requires careful planning of workflow selection order

questions.recommendation-rationale: The success criteria explicitly requires 'All action scripts in .rdd/src/actions/ have ≥80% test coverage'. Action scripts implement critical framework operations (prompt management, requirement CRUD, execution mode). Prioritizing them ensures we meet the primary goal, and their unit tests are faster to implement than integration tests.
